_comment: Frozen retrieval baselines. A drop of more than `tolerance` below `value`
fails CI. Update deliberately, in the same PR that causes the change, with
the paired-bootstrap delta in the commit message — never to make a red
Measured on the 42-paper frozen corpus with 472 ICT queries, hash
embeddings, retrieval scoped to one paper (matching production).
REVISED after a leak fix. The first version of these numbers was measured
with only the gold chunk redacted, which made it identifiable by length
alone: the chunker caps chunks at 110 words, so 88.9% of untouched chunks
sat at the cap and 0% of redacted gold chunks did. Ranking by length while
ignoring the query entirely scored nDCG@10 = 0.369, beating BM25's 0.224.
queries.redact_pool now removes one sentence from every candidate, which
tolerance is 0.005, not the CI half-width (~0.028). The point estimate is
deterministic — same corpus, same queries, no sampling in retrieval — so
run-to-run variance is zero and the gate only absorbs rounding.

leak_guard._comment: Ranking by chunk length alone must not beat random ordering.
